name: Music and media library
plain: Reads the person's own music library and listening history.
meaning: Reveals taste, play counts and playlists; on iOS it also gates Apple Music playback control.

android.prompt_ui: Allow or Don't allow music and audio
android.revocation: Settings > Apps > Permissions > Music and audio
android.note: No Spotify or YouTube Music library API exists at the OS level

ios.prompt_ui: Allow or Don't Allow access to Media and Apple Music
ios.revocation: Settings > Privacy & Security > Media & Apple Music
ios.note: Required for MPMediaLibrary and MusicKit playback

limits.headline: Can see your own music library and play your songs once you tap Allow
limits.user_action: You tap Allow when a music or player app asks for your library
can: List songs and playlists in your music library
Play your music inside the app
Use Apple Music playback on iPhone after the Media and Apple Music prompt
Use your audio files on Android after the music and audio prompt
cannot: Open Spotify or YouTube Music libraries; no phone wide access exists
See your listening history on Android, which does not keep it for apps
Use MusicKit or the media library on iPhone without the prompt
See photos or videos with this permission
limits.differs: iPhone uses the Media and Apple Music prompt. Android uses the music and audio prompt on Android 13 and newer.

story.what_it_is: Lets an app see your own music library and what you have listened to.

marketing.name: MusicKit
marketing.pitch: Developer pitch: let apps play Apple Music and read a person's music library with their permission.

story.for_you: A pop up asks to access your music library. If you say yes, the app can see your songs, playlists and play counts. On iPhone it can also control Apple Music playback.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to build playlists, show your history and suggest songs. It gives a rich picture of your taste, so permission matters.

use_cases.example: A music player shows your whole library and lets you pick songs from it.
A running app builds a playlist that matches your pace from songs you already own.
A rhythm game turns songs in your library into playable levels.
A DJ app mixes tracks from your library on a virtual deck.
A social app shows your top songs on your profile.
An ad firm could read your taste to guess age, mood and interests.
A car app lets you pick a song by voice from your own library.

story.android_note: Reads audio files with READ_MEDIA_AUDIO on newer Android.
story.ios_note: Needs the Media Library permission and also gates Apple Music playback control.

technical_bounds: Streaming service libraries are not exposed through the OS

history.change: Media library usage key and prompt introduced
